Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
236 PM EDT Tue Aug 4 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 234 PM EDT Tuesday...

No significant changes we made to the forecast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 234 PM EDT Tuesday...

1. Dry and calm conditions will continue this afternoon into 
tomorrow with high pressure overhead. Shower and thunderstorm 
chances return Thursday and Friday with broad troughing 
approaching the region.

2. Bermuda high set up will keep our region warm and with 
chances for showers from Friday night through Tuesday. 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 234 PM EDT Tuesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Tranquil weather is expected to continue tonight into 
tomorrow with high pressure in place overhead. Skies will remain 
clear and dry this evening into tonight with lows overnight in the 
upper 50s to low 60s. A few more protected valleys in the 
Adirondacks and NEK could see some lower 50s tonight with better 
radiational cooling. Tomorrow will be equally as pleasant as today, 
though with slightly more terrain driven fair weather cumulus. Our 
area of high pressure will shift a little south and east allowing 
for better southerly flow and moisture advection. Temperatures will 
be a degree or two warmer than today in the mid to low to mid 80s. 
Dewpoints will also be on the increase around 60. In the decoupled 
valleys tonight some patchy fog may be possible.

Our calm pattern will erode by Thursday. A Bermuda high responsible 
for our calm weather today will begin to shift slightly to the 
south with the return of troughing. Broad cyclonic flow by the 
end of the week will allow for better moisture advection into 
the region with a few shortwaves moving through. Temperatures 
Thursday will rise into the mid to upper 80s with dewpoints 
around 70 degrees. Heat indices will rise into the upper 80s to 
around 90 as a result. There does not look to be any real 
defined boundary for shower activity, but shortwaves Thursday 
and Friday look to bring enough energy to support shower and 
thunderstorm chances both afternoons. CAMs denote terrain 
instability around 1000-1500J/kg with around 20-30 knots of 
shear. CAPE and shear profiles will be supportive of a few 
thunderstorms across the Adirondacks. Should ingredients align 
Thursday, there is a chance for some stronger storms, primarily 
in northern New York, given good instability. Weaker shear 
profiles do lend some uncertainty to the strength of any storms 
in addition to weaker mid level lapse rates. By Friday, 
southwesterly flow and shear will increase to 30-40knots with 
similar instability levels, expanding into the northern 
Champlain Valley as well. Afternoon scattered showers and 
thunderstorms are anticipated, mainly over the terrain. A few 
stronger storms Friday may also be possible, especially with 
better shear and mid level lapse rates. Any storms will wane 
with the loss of diurnal heating in the evenings.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Bermuda high remains in place through the entirety of 
the extended portion of our forecast from Friday night through 
Tuesday. This will mean warm temperatures and active weather for 
northern New York and Vermont. Current model predictions are for 
Saturday to be the wettest day of the period, and Sunday to be the 
warmest. Tough to time fine scale features this far out without a 
significant synoptic feature. But, there are indications that upper 
level troughs and shortwave energy passing through will bring 
chances for showers more days than not. Looking further out we could 
have a pattern change towards the end of next week. Highs in the 80s 
and lows in the 60s for the extended period.

&&

.AVIATION /18Z TUESDAY THROUGH SUNDAY/...
Through 18Z Wednesday...Very quiet aviation forecast today with
mainly clear skies in place across the region as well as light 
winds. May see some fog formation in the typically fog prone 
spots from 06-13z. For now only included some BR at SLK and MPV.
